title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets) for P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. He studies the group T_{0,3} of conformal and anticonformal automorphisms of (P^1_C, {0,1,∞}) and its lifts to automorphisms of the fundamental group π_{0,3}. These are the topological, real-structure analogues of the generators and relations that later define Drinfeld's GT.

Part I, the Coxeter picture.
- Four great circles are drawn on the Riemann sphere:
  - the equator P^1_R (fixed circle of τ: z ↦ z̄);
  - three meridians through the poles -j̄ = e^{iπ/3} and -j = e^{-iπ/3}, namely the circles |z-1|=1, |z|=1 and Re z=1/2.
- These are the mirrors of the anti-involutions τ'_0 = z̄/(z̄-1), τ'_1 = 1/z̄ and τ'_∞ = 1-z̄.
- They cut the sphere into 12 spherical triangles. This is the barycentric subdivision of the two hemispheres, each viewed as a triangle with vertices 0, 1, ∞. The barycentres are the poles, and the edge midpoints are 1/2, 2, -1.
- The 12 triangles are fundamental domains, permuted simply transitively by T_{0,3} ≅ S_3 × Z/2 (order 12).
- Take the triangle (-j̄, 0, 1/2). Its angles are π/3 at the pole, π/2 at 0 and π/2 at 1/2.
- The reflections in its sides are τ (side 0–1/2), τ'_0 (side -j̄–0) and τ'_∞ (side -j̄–1/2). They give a Coxeter presentation of type (2,2,3), i.e. A_1×A_2 ≅ Z/2 × S_3:
  τ² = τ'_∞² = τ'_0² = (ττ'_∞)² = (τ'_0τ'_∞)³ = (ττ'_0)² = 1,
  with ττ'_∞ = σ_∞ = (1-z), ττ'_0 = σ_0 = z/(z-1), and τ'_0τ'_∞ = ρ^{-1} = 1 - 1/z.
- The orientation-preserving subgroup T^+ = S_3 is generated by σ_0, σ_∞ and ρ (relations (12)).

Part II.
- π_{0,3} = ⟨l_0, l_1, l_∞ | l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1⟩.
- Consider the index-2 subgroup S'_3 = {(g, τ^ε) : sgn(g) = (-1)^ε} = {1, τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞, ρ, ρ^{-1}}. This is a dihedral D_3 ≅ S_3, distinct from T^+.
- It is the stabilizer of the pole -j̄; equivalently of the upper half-plane, since the meridian reflections preserve Im z.
- Because it fixes a base point, it acts on π_{0,3} by genuine automorphisms, not merely outer ones.
- The notation is changed: what were τ̇_i become τ'_i (margin NB). The letters τ_i are thereby freed for the lifts of complex conjugation constructed on the next page, where τ_i = σ_iτ'_i, τ_i² = 1 and τ_∞τ_1 = l_0, etc.
- This exhibits ⟨τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞⟩ ≅ Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 as an extension of ⟨τ⟩ ≅ Z/2 by π_{0,3}. Its orientation-preserving words form π_{0,3}, of index 2.
errors: Relation (12) as written, σ̇_0 ρ σ̇_∞ = 1, is false with the page's own definitions. With σ_0 = z/(z-1), σ_∞ = 1-z and ρ = 1/(1-z) one computes σ_0 ρ σ_∞ = ρ. The correct relation is σ_0 σ_∞ ρ = 1 (equivalently σ_0σ_∞ = ρ^{-1}, which follows from (11)). The order of the letters is wrong.
In (12), 'σ̇²' is missing its subscript; it should read σ̇_∞² = 1.
The stabilizer is written (T_{0,3})_{J̄}; it should be the stabilizer of the pole -j̄ (consistent with the triangle (-j̄, 0, 1/2)).

Notational inconsistency with the previous page: there τσ̇_i was called τ̇_i and also τ̇'_i. Here the list of elements of S'_3 uses τ̇_i while their actions are called τ'_i. The margin NB acknowledges this renaming.
Previous page's figure labels the lower pole j, but the second fixed point of ρ is -j.

ideas.what: Four great circles (equator plus three meridians) give a tessellation of the Riemann sphere into 12 triangles with angles (π/2, π/2, π/3), on which Aut^±(P^1, {0,1,∞}) acts simply transitively; this is the barycentric subdivision of the two-hemisphere triangulation.
ideas.modern_name: Coxeter/reflection group of type (2,2,3); barycentric subdivision of the dessin of P^1 minus 3 points; extended anharmonic group
ideas.where_published: barycentric subdivisions of dessins appear in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific picture is unsure

ideas.what: Index-2 'twisted' subgroup S'_3 = {(g, τ^ε) : sgn g = (-1)^ε}, the stabilizer of the symmetric base point -j̄ (equivalently of the upper half-plane), acting by honest automorphisms on π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}, -j̄).
ideas.modern_name: dihedral symmetry group fixing a symmetric base point; real/anti-holomorphic automorphisms acting on the fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. work on real structures and GT (Drinfeld's GT includes complex conjugation λ = -1)
ideas.where_published: possibly in the Malgoire-referenced material [C] / La Longue Marche part I

ideas.what: Preparation for lifting complex conjugation to involutions τ_i of π_{0,3} with τ_∞τ_1 = l_0, etc., giving π_{0,3} as an index-2 subgroup of Z/2*Z/2*Z/2.
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group of the real quotient [P^1_C/τ]; real structures on π_1, complex conjugation in GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (reflection groups / Γ(2)); arithmetic version: Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but classical set-up: a Coxeter presentation of the order-12 extended symmetry group and the base-point-stabilizing dihedral subgroup acting on π_{0,3}. It contains a small slip in relation (12). Nothing appears that is absent from the literature; the more interesting lifting of complex conjugation is on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Top of page: page number 332 (internal numbering of the 'Deuxième partie').
In the list of elements of S'_3, the manuscript writes τ̇_0, τ̇, τ̇_∞ (first-pass notation), later renamed τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞.
Margin NB is roughly: 'NB τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞ [notation] ... notés précédemment τ̇_0, ...'. It records the renaming of τ̇_i to τ̇'_i; the exact wording is uncertain.
'Z/2' in T_{0,3} ≃ S_3 × Z/2 is correct; the image reads Z_{/2}, not Z/12.
